title: Assessment of Nutritional Status and Malnutrition
shortDescription: ABCD of assessment, anthropometric indices and the causes and prevention of malnutrition.
genZNote: If it can't be measured, it can't be fixed — ABCD is the nutrition audit. Stunting = long-term, wasting = recent. Don't swap them.

table.caption: ABCD (+E)
rows: Weight, height/length, BMI, MUAC, head/chest circumference, skinfold, waist–hip ratio
Haemoglobin, serum retinol, ferritin, albumin, urinary iodine
Physical signs: Bitot's spots, goitre, oedema, angular stomatitis
24-hour recall, food frequency questionnaire, weighed intake, food balance sheets
Mortality, morbidity, food availability, socio-economic factors

sections.heading: Anthropometric Indices
bullets: Weight-for-age → underweight; height-for-age → stunting (chronic); weight-for-height → wasting (acute); each < −2 SD of WHO Child Growth Standards.

MUAC 6–59 months: <11.5 cm = severe acute malnutrition (SAM), 11.5–12.5 cm = moderate; BMI adults: <18.5 underweight, 18.5–24.9 normal, ≥25 overweight (Asian cut-offs: ≥23 overweight, ≥27.5 obese in WHO Asia-Pacific).
Kwashiorkor: protein deficiency with oedema, flaky-paint dermatosis, fatty liver; Marasmus: severe energy deficit, wasting, "old-man" face; marasmic kwashiorkor combines both.

sections.heading: Causes and Prevention of Malnutrition
bullets: Causes: inadequate food and poverty, poor feeding and weaning practices, infections (diarrhoea, worms), low maternal education, lack of sanitation/safe water, low birth weight, food insecurity and climate shocks.

Prevention: first 1000 days (exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months, timely complementary feeding), growth monitoring, immunisation, micronutrient supplementation and fortification, safe water and sanitation, social safety nets (PDS, ICDS, PM POSHAN), nutrition education, treatment of SAM at Nutrition Rehabilitation Centres.
Double burden: stunting/anaemia alongside overweight and NCDs. NFHS-5 (2019–21): stunting ~35.5%, wasting ~19.3%, underweight ~32.1% among under-5 children (check later surveys).

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Nutritional status is assessed through anthropometric, biochemical, clinical and dietary methods, and malnutrition is prevented through dietary, health, sanitation and social interventions.

commonTraps: Do not confuse stunting with wasting.

confusedTerms.distinction: Kwashiorkor: protein deficiency with oedema; marasmus: overall energy deficiency with severe wasting and no oedema.
